# zheevx

> Computes the eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right eigenvectors for Hermitian matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zheevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zheevx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zheevx(
    order,
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK,
    RWORK,
    IWORK,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'`: Compute eigenvalues only; `'compute-vectors'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors. |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | `'all'`: all eigenvalues will be found. `'value'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (VL,VU] will be found. `'index'`: the IL-th through IU-th eigenvalues will be found. |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'`: Upper triangle of A is stored; `'lower'`: Lower triangle of A is stored. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix A.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. On exit, the lower triangle (if `uplo === 'lower'`) or the upper triangle (if `uplo === 'upper'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `vl` | `number` | If `range === 'value'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. |
| `vu` | `number` | If `range === 'value'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues.<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | If `range === 'index'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0.<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | If `range === 'index'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. 1 <= IL <= IU <= N, if N > 0.<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · On normal exit, the first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order. |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| `Z` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · If `jobz === 'compute-vectors'`, then if INFO = 0, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with W(i). |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z`<br>Rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ LWKMIN</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least the reference's minimum `LWKMIN` elements (`1` when `N <= 1`, `2*N` otherwise); if `null`, a workspace of the reference's optimal size (LWKOPT, with the ZHETRD block size from `ilaenv`) is allocated |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 7 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `7 * N` elements |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `5 * N` elements |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · If `jobz === 'compute-vectors'`, then if INFO = 0, the first M elements of IFAIL are zero (0-based). |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | Stride length for `IFAIL` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found.
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found.
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A. On exit, the lower triangle (if `UPLO='L'`) or the upper triangle (if `UPLO='U'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing A to tridiagonal form.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

  See "Computing Small Singular Values of Bidiagonal Matrices with Guaranteed High Relative Accuracy," by Demmel and Kahan, LAPACK Working Note #3.
- `m`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: On normal exit, the first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If an eigenvector fails to converge, then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.
- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` ninth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` seventeenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)
- `RangeError` seventeenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < max( 1, range === "index" ? iu - il + 1 : N ) )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zheevx.ndarray(
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL, offsetIFAIL
) → integer
```

Computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a complex.
Hermitian matrix A.

Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying a range of values
(RANGE='value') or a range of indices (RANGE='index') for the desired
eigenvalues.

Algorithm:
1. Scale the matrix if the norm is outside safe range
2. Reduce to tridiagonal form via zhetrd
3. If computing all eigenvalues with abstol <= 0:
   - JOBZ='no-vectors': dsterf for eigenvalues only
   - JOBZ='compute-vectors': zungtr + zsteqr for eigenvalues+eigenvectors
4. Otherwise (selective):
   - dstebz for selected eigenvalues by bisection
   - zstein for eigenvectors by inverse iteration (if JOBZ='compute-vectors')
   - zunmtr to transform back to original space
5. Sort eigenvalues and eigenvectors, undo scaling

M is an output parameter indicating the number of eigenvalues found.
It is returned via the out object: out.M.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | 'no-vectors' or 'compute-vectors' |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | 'all', 'value', or 'index' |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | 'upper' or 'lower' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output Hermitian matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A (complex elements) |
| `vl` | `number` | Lower bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | Upper bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value')<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | Index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | Index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | Absolute tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride for w |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for w |
| `Z` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvector matrix (N x N) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of Z (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of Z (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for Z (complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ LWKMIN</sub> | **out** · Complex workspace (length from `offsetWork` at least the reference's minimum, `1` when `N <= 1` and `2*N` otherwise; `(NB+1)*N`, with `NB` the ZHETRD block size from `ilaenv`, is optimal) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK (complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 7 * N</sub> | **out** · Real workspace (length from `offsetRWork` at least `7*N`, the reference's declared extent) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | Stride for RWORK |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for RWORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Integer workspace (length from `offsetIWork` at least `5*N`, the reference's declared extent) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | Stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for IWORK |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | Stride for IFAIL |
| ↳ `offsetIFAIL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for IFAIL |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found.
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found.
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the Hermitian matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of A contains the upper triangular part of the matrix A. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of A contains the lower triangular part of the matrix A. On exit, the lower triangle (if `UPLO='L'`) or the upper triangle (if `UPLO='U'`) of A, including the diagonal, is destroyed.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing A to tridiagonal form.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

  See "Computing Small Singular Values of Bidiagonal Matrices with Guaranteed High Relative Accuracy," by Demmel and Kahan, LAPACK Working Note #3.
- `m`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: On normal exit, the first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If an eigenvector fails to converge, then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.

- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` WORK, RWORK and IWORK must be sufficiently large

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, then i eigenvectors failed to converge. Their indices are stored in array `IFAIL`.

</section>

## Notes

-   `zheevx()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZHEEVX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zheevx.f).

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import zheevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zheevx';

// All eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a 3x3 Hermitian matrix A (column-major):
const N = 3;
let A = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 5.0, 0.0, 0.0, -2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 6.0, 0.0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );
const w = new Float64Array( N );
const Z = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 64 * N );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 7 * N );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 5 * N );
const IFAIL = new Int32Array( N );

// Using the standard interface:
let info = zheevx( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'upper', N, A, N, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, m, w, 1, Z, N, WORK, RWORK, IWORK, IFAIL, 1 );
console.log( 'info:', info, 'm:', m[ 0 ], 'eigenvalues:', w );

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 5.0, 0.0, 0.0, -2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 6.0, 0.0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
info = zheevx.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'upper', N, A, 1, N, 0, 0.0, 0.0, 1, N, 0.0, m, w, 1, 0, Z, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0, RWORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0, IFAIL, 1, 0 );
console.log( 'info:', info, 'm:', m[ 0 ], 'eigenvalues:', w );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZHEEVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZHEEVX computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a complex Hermitian matrix A. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either a range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

</section>
